item.title: Kerberos channel binding guidance adds Graph enforcement and CBT prerequisites — 26 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 26 November 2026

Kerberos channel binding guidance adds Graph enforcement and CBT prerequisites

A new Entra ID how-to covers channel binding for Kerberos-based Microsoft Entra Seamless SSO, including prerequisites and enforcement through Microsoft Graph. Other substantive updates clarify Global Secure Access probe configuration, cross-tenant synchronization recovery, and PIM audit correlation.

Entra ID · Authentication

New Kerberos channel-binding procedure specifies enforcement prerequisites

The new how-to explains channel binding for Kerberos-based Microsoft Entra Seamless SSO and enforcement through Microsoft Graph. It identifies client CBT support, TLS paths, Graph permissions, and policy propagation as rollout checks.

Global Secure Access · Monitoring

Global Secure Access health-probe guidance changes the port to 6543

The Remote Network Resilience page now specifies port 6543 instead of 6544 for the health-probe endpoint. Configure the IP SLA Layer 7 health probe with port 6543.

External ID · Provisioning

Cross-tenant sync guidance addresses soft-deleted target users

The configuration guidance explains that incremental synchronization may not reprocess a target-tenant soft deletion. For same-cloud synchronization, it recommends on-demand provisioning for the affected source user; manual restoration in the target tenant remains an option.

ID Governance · Governance

PIM audit guidance adds request-ID correlation across asynchronous flows

The updated guidance explains that related group membership and ownership activation or deactivation events can have different CorrelationId values. It documents using roleAssignmentRequestId and Log Analytics queries to trace the complete workflow.

item.title: Multitenant Entra app guidance details explicit tenant IDs and impact reports — 25 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 25 November 2026

Multitenant Entra app guidance details explicit tenant IDs and impact reports

New Entra ID guidance describes restricting multitenant apps to explicitly listed tenant IDs, with enablement through the Microsoft 365 or Entra admin center and reports to identify existing unrestricted apps. Authentication guidance now directs administrators to Baseline Security Mode for password-credential blocking. Four ID Governance preview pages add Microsoft 365 E7 licensing language, and the Contentstack provisioning tutorial has been removed.

Entra ID · Security

New guidance describes tenant allowlists for multitenant apps

The guidance describes requiring multitenant apps to explicitly allow listed tenant IDs. It points administrators to the Microsoft 365 or Entra admin center to enable the setting and to reports for identifying existing unrestricted apps. If enabled, administrators should review the impact report before restricting existing app audiences.

Entra ID · Authentication

Password-blocking guidance points to Baseline Security Mode

The page now directs administrators to Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Org settings > Security and Privacy > Baseline Security Mode to enable the password-credential blocking setting. It also adds access guidance and updates the app policy link.

ID Governance · Governance

ID Governance preview guidance names Microsoft 365 E7 for access

Updated App Roles Assign and PIM guidance specifies a Microsoft 365 E7 license plan for preview access. The material says capabilities may change, licensing requirements for agents and agent identities are not yet announced or finalized, and existing assignment-management permissions remain unchanged.

Entra ID · Provisioning

Contentstack provisioning tutorial is no longer available

The Microsoft Entra tutorial covering automatic user provisioning and deprovisioning with Contentstack was removed, so its documented setup steps are no longer available at that URL.

View all updates for 25 November 2026 →

item.title: Tenant Restrictions proxy guidance adds sign-in hosts and device-authentication exclusions — 24 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 24 November 2026

Tenant Restrictions proxy guidance adds sign-in hosts and device-authentication exclusions

Tenant Restrictions receives the period’s clearest operational guidance: Microsoft sign-in host names, the required tenant restrictions v2 header for proxy enforcement, and exclusions for device-authentication hosts are now documented. Other updates clarify PIM coverage for agents and agent identities, Verified ID Key Vault permissions, SMB administrative-share limitations, and self-approval risks in dynamic approval callbacks. The changes refine configuration and security guidance rather than announce a new service launch.

Entra ID · General

Tenant Restrictions guidance specifies proxy hosts, headers, and authentication exclusions

The configuration guidance adds Microsoft sign-in host names, states that proxy enforcement requires the tenant restrictions v2 header, and lists device-authentication hosts to exclude from TLS inspection and header injection. Review proxy rules against these details to preserve device authentication.

ID Governance · Governance

PIM documentation maps support for agents and agent identities

The updated page adds a matrix covering users, groups, agents, and agent identities across PIM providers, including preview and E7 license details. It also clarifies provider selection and agent-access references; administrators can use the matrix when configuring PIM.

ID Governance · Governance

Dynamic approval callbacks can return the requester as approver

The guidance now explains that a callback may return the access requester as an approver, potentially allowing self-approval, while built-in approval options prevent it. Review callback logic where dynamic approval is used.

Verified ID · Security

Verified ID setup changes the documented Key Vault permission prerequisite

Advanced setup guidance no longer requires the Key Vault Access Policy permission model. It says the vault’s creator account needs permission to create, delete, and sign with keys; verify those permissions for the account performing setup.

Entra ID · General

Entra group assignments do not cover SMB administrative shares

The device-management guidance now states that groups assigned through this policy do not apply to SMB administrative shares such as C$ and Admin$, in addition to remote desktop connections. An individual user’s SID must be added to grant those permissions.

View all updates for 24 November 2026 →

item.title: BYOT SMS and voice guidance expands as Authenticator passkey timing shifts — 23 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 23 November 2026

BYOT SMS and voice guidance expands as Authenticator passkey timing shifts

The period’s main development is a new Bring Your Own Telephony (BYOT) deployment guide for SMS and voice authentication, alongside broader BYOT coverage in existing CYOT guidance. Authenticator passkey documentation now limits attested-passkey registration to direct in-app flows and places the Credential Registration resource’s availability in January 2027 rather than late November 2026. Global Secure Access preview guidance also describes a broader AI-agent discovery inventory. Most other changes are navigation or terminology updates, including renamed telephony-provider links and standardized ID Protection wording.

Entra ID · Authentication

New BYOT guide details API-based SMS and voice deployment

A new Entra ID guide explains how to deploy a telephony provider’s BYOT integration in an Azure subscription and configure SMS and voice authentication through Microsoft Graph APIs. It covers prerequisites, permissions, deployment, policy configuration, and testing.

Entra ID · Authentication

Existing telephony guidance now covers BYOT alongside CYOT

The telephony-fraud article now covers both models, with fraud protection, destination, spending, and monitoring guidance applying to BYOT as well as CYOT. It also adds BYOT API setup, provider-support details, and updated FAQ navigation.

Entra ID · Authentication

Attested passkeys require direct Authenticator registration

The passkey support guidance now states that users can register attested passkeys only directly in the Microsoft Authenticator app; cross-device registration flows do not support attested passkeys.

Entra ID · Conditional Access

Credential Registration resource guidance moves availability to January 2027

The Authenticator passkey guidance now says the Microsoft Authenticator Credential Registration resource will be available in January 2027 instead of late November 2026. Provisioning its enterprise application remains required before excluding it from a Conditional Access policy.

Global Secure Access · Fundamentals

Global Secure Access preview guidance expands AI-agent discovery coverage

The preview documentation now describes discovery of managed, shadow, and unclassified AI agents, including local agents and Copilot Studio cloud agents. It also covers attribution, connected model providers and MCP servers, destinations, and traffic volume.

View all updates for 23 November 2026 →

item.title: Entra sets 2027 SMS and voice MFA retirement dates for users without passkey support — 20 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 20 November 2026

Entra sets 2027 SMS and voice MFA retirement dates for users without passkey support

The period’s most consequential change is a Microsoft Entra MFA retirement notice: users who rely solely on Microsoft-provided SMS or voice in sessions that do not support passkeys must register alternative methods or configure customer-managed telephony. Retirement begins February 1, 2027, with July 1, 2027 applying to admins and external users. A separate December rollout will change passkey registration in My Sign-ins. Agent ID guidance also becomes more operationally specific for CIMD and MCP integrations, while Copilot Studio’s Dataverse agent-user capability receives a December 8 general-availability date. Most other updates are routine documentation maintenance.

Entra ID · Conditional Access

SMS and voice MFA retirement now carries two 2027 preparation deadlines

Microsoft says users relying solely on Microsoft-provided SMS or voice for MFA in sessions that do not support passkeys must register alternative methods or configure customer-managed telephony. Retirement begins February 1, 2027; the notice lists July 1, 2027 for admins and external users. Early preparation is required to avoid sign-in blocks.

Entra ID · Authentication

My Sign-ins passkey registration gets a guided December rollout

For Microsoft Authenticator users, the My Sign-ins registration experience will add a checkbox, revised link text, and guided steps to start registration. Rollout begins in early December 2026 and completes by the end of December, so organizations should update user communications and internal procedures.

Agent ID · General

CIMD preview guidance specifies endpoint, scope, and token requirements

The updated Agent ID configuration guidance requires a nonempty MCP endpoint path without a trailing slash, fully qualified delegated scopes, and `organizations` for multitenant authorization servers. It identifies the resource application’s client-ID GUID as the token audience and says not to use client secrets or private-key assertions during preview. Review CIMD and MCP configurations to prevent token acquisition issues.

Agent ID · Monitoring

CIMD consent guidance distinguishes default, strict, and open postures

The CIMD client documentation now describes default, strict, and open tenant consent postures, including how approval and OAuth scopes behave. It warns that unrestricted consent can enable consent phishing and unauthorized data access; use the strict posture when client onboarding requires administrative review.

Agent ID · Provisioning

Copilot Studio Dataverse agent users receive a December 8 GA date

Microsoft announced that Copilot Studio will support creating Dataverse agent users with a Microsoft Entra agent’s user account at general availability on December 8, 2026. The announcement provides the availability date but specifies no additional administrator action.

View all updates for 20 November 2026 →

item.title: Deprecated memberOf processing leaves groups stale as MemberOf Next becomes the migration path — 19 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 19 November 2026

Deprecated memberOf processing leaves groups stale as MemberOf Next becomes the migration path

The earlier memberOf preview ended on November 3, 2026: configurations using it stop updating and remain in their last known state. Microsoft’s documented route forward is MemberOf Next, alongside the preview of Transitive Reports To; both require Microsoft Entra ID Governance, Standard priority, and scheduled twice-daily processing. The period also brings risk-based CAPTCHA for SMS and voice MFA, preview coverage for the Windows App desktop client in Conditional Access app protection, and refreshed FIDO2 attestation data.

Entra ID · General

The earlier memberOf preview has stopped updating configurations

Microsoft states that the earlier memberOf preview ended on November 3, 2026. Configurations using it stop updating and remain in their last known state; guidance directs administrators to migrate affected dynamic groups, administrative units, and entitlement management auto-assignment policies to MemberOf Next.

Entra ID · Monitoring

MemberOf Next and Transitive Reports To are documented in preview

MemberOf Next flattens members from selected groups, while Transitive Reports To includes a manager’s full reporting hierarchy. Both support dynamic groups and administrative units and can scope governance controls. They require Microsoft Entra ID Governance, Standard priority, and scheduled twice-daily updates, so membership changes may not appear immediately.

Entra ID · Authentication

Risk-based CAPTCHA is being added to SMS and voice MFA

Starting in mid-November 2026, Microsoft Entra ID will add risk-based CAPTCHA verification to SMS and voice MFA to counter automated fraud. Some users may need to complete CAPTCHA before receiving codes or calls, requiring help-desk preparation, user communications, network readiness, and continued adoption of phishing-resistant methods.

Entra ID · Conditional Access

Windows App desktop client joins Windows MAM preview guidance

Conditional Access guidance now includes the Windows App desktop client as a preview target for Windows MAM and app protection policies, with links to configuration requirements and supported scenarios. Administrators evaluating the capability should review those requirements and environments before configuring policies.

Entra ID · Authentication

FIDO2 attestation data adds 18 security-key models

The attestation table now references MDS version 297 instead of 285 and adds 18 FIDO2 security-key models with their AAGUIDs and capability indicators. The refreshed list supports eligibility and capability checks when evaluating keys.

View all updates for 19 November 2026 →

item.title: Native Authentication V2 guidance now separates browser domain requirements from mobile clients — 18 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 18 November 2026

Native Authentication V2 guidance now separates browser domain requirements from mobile clients

The 18 November updates were dominated by documentation revisions, but several have practical administrator value: Embedded Native Authentication V2 guidance defines the browser-versus-native domain split and lists MSAL.js 5.29.1; SSPR writeback guidance covers PHS staged rollout with Cloud Sync; PIM and Windows Server with Intune preview scope is clearer; and Global Secure Access now states concrete cloud-firewall limits. Remaining edits mainly refine terminology, navigation, links, or examples.

Entra ID · Authentication

Embedded Native Authentication V2 migration clarifies browser domains and MSAL.js minimum

The migration page now states that browser-based apps require a tenant-verified custom domain, while native Android and iOS clients can use their configured service authority without a custom domain or CORS proxy. It sets the listed MSAL.js minimum at 5.29.1.

Entra ID · Authentication

SSPR writeback guidance documents PHS staged rollout with Cloud Sync

The on-premises password writeback page now states that SSPR password writeback is supported for users in PHS staged rollout when Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync is used.

ID Governance · Fundamentals

PIM guidance documents preview agent access and Bastion session controls

The identity governance overview now covers PIM preview support for just-in-time Azure resource access by agents and agent identities, along with Azure Bastion session analytics, recordings, and session disconnection.

Entra ID · Conditional Access

Windows Server with Intune preview guidance flags possible automatic enrollment

The Arc sign-in guide now links to the current preview resource and says qualifying devices might be automatically enrolled when the Entra extension is deployed. Administrators evaluating the preview are directed to review its scope and enrollment guidance.

Global Secure Access · General

Global Secure Access cloud firewall documents tenant and per-rule limits

The current limitations page now states that cloud firewall supports up to 1,000 rules per tenant and a combined total of 500 sources and destinations per rule.

View all updates for 18 November 2026 →

item.title: Identity verification guidance now spans risk remediation, onboarding, and account recovery — 17 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 17 November 2026

Identity verification guidance now spans risk remediation, onboarding, and account recovery

The strongest administrator signal is a coordinated identity-verification guidance set. A new Conditional Access guide covers resource access, onboarding, account recovery, and risk scenarios, while ID Protection guidance documents the Require Identity Verification preview control for User risk and Sign-in risk. A separate Entra ID update records that the earlier memberOf preview ended on November 3, 2026, leaving dependent configurations at their last known state. Authentication-methods guidance adds concrete policy limits, and Agent ID documents a tightly bounded Client ID Metadata Document preview.

Entra ID · Conditional Access

Conditional Access guide maps identity verification across administrator journeys

New Entra ID guidance explains how to configure and test identity verification for resource access, onboarding, account recovery, and risk-based scenarios. It includes prerequisites, eligible profiles, pilot setup, emergency-access exclusions, and policy ordering.

ID Protection · Conditional Access

Risk-policy guidance details Require Identity Verification as a preview control

Updated ID Protection guidance covers the Require Identity Verification control for User risk and Sign-in risk conditions. The control requires an eligible identity verification profile and supported credential; successful verification remediates the applicable risk, while failed verification does not.

Entra ID · General

Retired memberOf preview leaves affected configurations frozen

The earlier memberOf preview ended on November 3, 2026. Dynamic groups, dynamic administrative units, and entitlement management auto-assignment policies using it no longer update and remain in their last known state; the guidance directs administrators to MemberOf Next.

Entra ID · Authentication

Authentication methods guidance documents a 20 KB policy limit

Updated Entra ID guidance describes removal of individual-user targeting and a 20 KB policy-size limit. It also adds preview detail about passkey credential assurance and provenance, identity-verification history, and the possibility of registration or policy-save failures for policies targeting individual users or many groups.

Agent ID · Standards

Agent ID documents public-metadata client IDs for delegated token requests

A new preview guide explains how a public HTTPS Client ID Metadata Document URL can serve as an OAuth or MCP client ID for requesting delegated Microsoft Entra tokens without prior registration. The pattern requires authorization code flow with PKCE, may require administrator consent, has no service-level agreement, and is not recommended for production workloads.

item.title: MFA now prioritizes non-telephony methods ahead of February 2027 SMS retirement — 11 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 11 November 2026

MFA now prioritizes non-telephony methods ahead of February 2027 SMS retirement

Microsoft Entra’s most consequential change is the October 2026 MFA rollout: non-telephony methods are presented first, while SMS and voice remain under “Show more verification methods” ahead of their planned February 2027 retirement. GoTo provisioning also has a March 31, 2027 migration deadline, and a cross-tenant synchronization caveat can leave removed users in the target tenant. Most other updates are documentation maintenance, including standardized “telephony provider” terminology, revised provisioning OAuth-consent steps, and clearer report-freshness and consent guidance.

Entra ID · Authentication

MFA flows prioritize non-telephony verification methods

The October 2026 rollout places more secure non-telephony methods ahead of SMS and voice. SMS and voice remain available under “Show more verification methods,” and users should expect a resend waiting period. Microsoft says no configuration change is required and advises planning for SMS and voice retirement in February 2027.

Entra ID · Provisioning

GoTo provisioning requires an OAuth grant migration

The GoTo automatic-provisioning tutorial now requires an OAuth client using Client Credentials Grant because Authorization Code Grant is being retired. Affected provisioning jobs must migrate by March 31, 2027 or user and group synchronization may stop; SSO is unaffected.

Entra ID · Provisioning

Cross-tenant sync can retain users after scope removal

The known-issues guidance says users removed from a cross-tenant synchronization job’s scope are not deleted from the target tenant if the job is restarted before the next synchronization cycle. Administrators should let that cycle complete before restarting the job.

Entra ID · Provisioning

Provisioning OAuth consent guidance moves into Azure portal

The Box provisioning tutorial now directs administrators to sign in to the Azure portal, open Microsoft Entra ID > Enterprise applications, and follow added OAuth-consent guidance. Similar partner provisioning tutorials received the same portal-navigation treatment during the period.

Entra ID · General

Inactive guest reports now show freshness timestamps

The inactive guest report now displays when it was last updated and refreshes once per day. Its guest count can differ from current tenant totals and from the ID Governance dashboard or Users blade, so administrators should use the timestamp when comparing views.

item.title: Passkey guidance now separates password changes from lost-passkey account recovery — 10 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 10 November 2026

Passkey guidance now separates password changes from lost-passkey account recovery

The strongest updates clarify Entra ID authentication and dynamic-group behavior rather than announce new releases. The period also adds explicit Conditional Access Policy Plans limits and expands Global Secure Access private network connector operational guidance.

Entra ID · Authentication

Forgotten-password and lost-passkey paths are now documented separately

The SSPR how-it-works guidance now says a user who signs in with a passkey can change a forgotten password without entering the current password. Losing the passkey is a separate path requiring account recovery or administrator-issued recovery credentials to register a new one.

Entra ID · Conditional Access

Conditional Access Policy Plans now state their scale limits

The guidance sets a limit of 100 rules per plan and 100 plans per tenant, while streamlining Global Secure Access and agent-access scenarios. Administrators can use these limits when designing and scaling policy plans.

Entra ID · General

Unsupported dynamic-group properties fail when processing resumes

The Groups Create Rule guidance says unsupported properties can be saved while processing is paused but produce a Processing error when processing resumes. Membership remains at the last successful evaluation and no new members are added, so affected users may not receive targeted policies or assignments.

Entra ID · General

Deleted child groups can leave memberOf membership unchanged

The memberOf dynamic-rule guidance now says deleting a child group does not automatically update membership: affected users or devices remain members until the rule is modified. Administrators should use this limitation when troubleshooting dynamic-group membership.

Global Secure Access · General

Private network connector notes expand diagnostics and security detail

Global Secure Access release notes now cover 24-hour CPU and memory history, improved health reporting, interface-specific DNS, trace rotation, expanded event-log capacity, clearer errors, TCP keepalive, memory management, and local log and file security. Administrators can download the version from the Microsoft Entra admin center to assess the operational improvements.

item.description:

Global Secure Access guidance moves QUIC handling to Custom Acquire and firewall blocking

Four Global Secure Access pages now align on a different QUIC operating pattern: keep browser QUIC enabled, acquire UDP 443 with Custom Acquire, and use a cloud firewall Block rule. item.title: Microsoft-provided SMS and voice SSPR retirement sets February 2027 recovery deadline — 3 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 3 November 2026

Microsoft-provided SMS and voice SSPR retirement sets February 2027 recovery deadline

Two Message Center notices carry the day’s main operational weight: Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication for self-service password reset begins retiring in February 2027, with a 50-day transition for each user group, while the Microsoft Entra Security Operator mapping in Defender for Office 365 changes starting December 2026. A new Private Access sign-in-every-time preview adds a Conditional Access-dependent reauthentication path. Most other entries are documentation maintenance or troubleshooting guidance, with notable Salesforce provisioning prerequisites and an RHEL upgrade warning.

Entra ID · Conditional Access

SMS and voice SSPR authentication begins retiring in February 2027

Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication for self-service password reset will retire beginning in February 2027. Each user group receives a 50-day transition, after which those methods will no longer be available for SSPR.

Entra ID · Security

Defender for Office 365 removes default Security Operator permissions

Starting in December 2026, the Unified RBAC mapping for the Microsoft Entra Security Operator role will remove default access to email threat policies and the Tenant/Allow Block List. Administrators must manually assign permissions if continued access is needed.

Private Access · Conditional Access

Private Access sign-in-every-time preview gets a pilot deployment guide

The new guide explains how to configure, test, and deploy reauthentication for selected private applications using one Conditional Access policy and a pilot group. It requires Global Secure Access Windows client version 2.34.222 or later.

Entra ID · Provisioning

Salesforce provisioning guidance adds SOAP login and API-auth prerequisites

The updated Entra provisioning tutorial requires Salesforce SOAP API `login()` to be enabled and the Admin Username account to have **Use Any API Auth**. It also documents Salesforce’s December 1, 2026 requirement and related credential-validation failures.

Entra ID · Authentication

RHEL upgrades can remove the Entra SSH sign-in extension

The Linux sign-in guidance now warns that in-place upgrades from RHEL 8.x to 9.x can remove the `aadsshlogin` package and cause `Permission denied (publickey)` errors. The documented remedy is to uninstall and reinstall the AADSSHLoginForLinux extension.

item.description:
Day in brief · 30 October 2026

Choose-your-own telephony reaches Entra GA before February 2027 SMS retirement

Authentication dominates this period: Choose Your Own Telephony Provider (CYOT) is generally available for Entra SMS and voice authentication, with Microsoft-provided services retiring on 1 February 2027. Supporting guidance now covers deployment, fraud controls, resiliency, and end-to-end troubleshooting, while the SMS sign-in page says “Enable first factor sign-in” automatically disables after 30 days without traffic. Passkey changes span profile migration, synced passkeys, Windows availability, and an External ID credential-management API; ID Governance also documents a preview for reviewing access packages as single catalog-review items.

Entra ID · Authentication

CYOT becomes generally available ahead of Microsoft-provided SMS and voice retirement

Microsoft Entra now generally supports Choose Your Own Telephony Provider for SMS and voice authentication. Microsoft-provided services retire on 1 February 2027, so organizations must select a provider, set up CYOT, and transition before that date. Microsoft recommends phishing-resistant methods such as passkeys.

Entra ID · Authentication

Passkey profiles and synced passkeys move to GA with tenant migration

An updated rollout notice sets general availability for passkey profiles and synced passkeys starting March 2026 for tenants with Passkeys (FIDO2) enabled. Existing tenants are automatically migrated to a default passkey profile; passkeyType is configurable, while registration-campaign settings and rollout timelines vary by cloud region.

Entra ID · Conditional Access

Windows passkeys reach GA without explicit administrator allow-listing

The Windows passkey notice sets general availability from late April 2026. The capability supports passwordless, phishing-resistant sign-in on corporate, personal, and shared Windows devices without explicit allow-listing; Authentication Methods policies and Conditional Access provide the controls, with administrator action needed if blocking is desired.

External ID · Authentication

External ID documents customer passkey credential-management API

A new API reference documents how signed-in External ID customers can list, register, and delete their own passkeys. An application must have a manually provisioned service principal and the required delegated permission; app-only tokens are not supported.

ID Governance · Governance

Catalog access reviews add access packages as preview review items

The ID Governance preview lets reviewers treat access packages as single items in catalog access reviews, approving or denying each package. A denial removes the assignment and all resources it grants at the review end date. Prerequisites include an eligible subscription, the Identity Governance Administrator role, and a catalog containing the packages.

item.title: Risk-based CAPTCHA expands Entra sign-in defenses as Cloud Sync guidance tightens prerequisites — 29 October 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 29 October 2026

Risk-based CAPTCHA expands Entra sign-in defenses as Cloud Sync guidance tightens prerequisites

Microsoft is rolling out risk-based CAPTCHA for SMS and voice first-factor sign-ins to curb automated abuse; the rollout began in mid-October and prompts depend on user behavior. The most actionable documentation updates make Cloud Sync enforcement prerequisites explicit, define the scope and limits of passwordless cloud-password changes, and clarify how Global Secure Access V2’s Continue action moves traffic across profiles. A new Agent ID tutorial covers PostgreSQL access for agents, while Authenticator usability improvements are scheduled from November 2026.

Entra ID · Authentication

Risk-based CAPTCHA reaches SMS and voice first-factor sign-ins

Microsoft Entra ID is adding risk-based CAPTCHA verification to SMS and voice first-factor sign-ins to reduce automated abuse. Rollout began in mid-October 2026, and users may see the challenge based on their behavior. Organizations should prepare help desks, review network requirements, and encourage phishing-resistant methods such as passkeys.

Entra ID · Provisioning

Cloud Sync enforcement now has explicit domain-controller and tool prerequisites

The updated guidance requires every writable domain controller to meet the specified Windows Server update levels and requires ADSyncTools version 2.6.0 or later. It warns that enforcement cannot be configured if any writable domain controller is unsupported.

Entra ID · Authentication

Passwordless SSPR guidance defines a tenant-wide secure sign-in setting

The updated SSPR deep dive documents cloud-password changes after authentication with a FIDO2 passkey or Windows Hello for Business credential, without the current password. It identifies a tenant-wide setting required to enable the experience, says it cannot be scoped to groups, and calls out a limitation involving on-premises password writeback.

Internet Access · Fundamentals

Global Secure Access V2 clarifies Continue’s cross-profile evaluation

The web-filtering guidance now describes Continue as a preview default action when no enabled enforcement rule matches. Continue passes evaluation to the next applicable security profile in priority order, while Allow and Block stop V2 evaluation; the examples also distinguish Baseline and V1 behavior.

Agent ID · Conditional Access

New Agent ID tutorial covers PostgreSQL authorization for agents

A new tutorial explains how to configure Microsoft Entra agent identities to authenticate to Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server and access data through group-based authorization, entitlement management, and Conditional Access. It covers prerequisites, Entra authentication, security groups, token exchange, and database permissions.

item.title: Qualifying Entra tenants face SMS first-factor sign-in disablement through November — 28 October 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 28 October 2026

Qualifying Entra tenants face SMS first-factor sign-in disablement through November

Microsoft will disable SMS first-factor sign-in in tenants with no successful or only unsuccessful SMS sign-ins during the previous 30 days, with rollout timing from mid-September through November 2026; SMS MFA and password reset remain unaffected. The period also documents an Agent ID inactivity-policy preview, sets a 31 March 2027 OAuth migration deadline for Vonage and Puzzel provisioning, gives Authenticator passkey setup November 2026 availability timing, and clarifies cross-tenant synchronization licensing.

Entra ID · Authentication

SMS first-factor sign-in faces disablement for low-use tenants

Microsoft says it will disable SMS first-factor sign-in in tenants with no successful or only unsuccessful SMS sign-ins in the past 30 days, with timing from mid-September through November 2026. SMS used for MFA and password reset is unaffected; administrators should review usage, notify users, and ensure alternate sign-in methods.

Agent ID · Governance

Agent ID preview policy sets 60-, 90-, and 455-day milestones

The preview policy notifies owners after 60 days of inactivity, disables identities after 90 days, and deletes them after 455 days. It can be enabled without a license, with configurable scope and fallback notification recipients; seasonal or limited-use agents should be excluded if they must remain inactive.

Entra ID · Provisioning

Vonage provisioning must move to OAuth client credentials by March 2027

Vonage provisioning will stop supporting OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code Grant after 31 March 2027. The revised procedure uses OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials Grant; affected user and group synchronization jobs should migrate by the deadline to avoid provisioning stoppage or eventual job removal. SSO is unaffected.

Entra ID · Conditional Access

Authenticator passkey setup guidance names November 2026 resource availability

The setup guidance states that the Microsoft Authenticator Credential Registration resource will be available in November 2026. Administrators must provision the enterprise application before excluding the resource from a Conditional Access policy.

ID Governance · Fundamentals

Cross-tenant group synchronization carries Governance or Suite licensing requirements

The updated guidance distinguishes direct user synchronization, which requires Microsoft Entra ID P1, from synchronizing a group and its members, which requires Microsoft Entra ID Governance or Microsoft Entra Suite for each synchronized user in the source tenant. Group-synchronization planners should verify those licenses.

Microsoft-provided SMS and voice face February 2027 Entra retirement deadline

Microsoft Entra ID will begin retiring Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication on February 1, 2027. Organizations must move users to passkeys or other authentication methods, or configure a customer-managed telecom provider, to avoid sign-in disruptions. The period also brings a planned MFA recognition change for Windows Hello for Business and macOS Platform SSO, alongside substantive preview guidance and limitations for Entra Internet Access cloud firewall deployments.

Entra ID · Authentication

Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication retirement

Microsoft Entra ID will retire Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication starting February 1, 2027. Administrators must migrate users to passkeys or other methods, or configure a customer-managed telecom provider; passkeys are recommended and migration is intended to prevent sign-in disruptions.

Entra ID · Conditional Access

Windows Hello and macOS Platform SSO become standalone MFA factors

Starting in early November 2026, Microsoft Entra will recognize Windows Hello for Business and macOS Platform SSO as standalone MFA factors, allowing users to satisfy MFA without an additional passkey. No configuration changes are required, but onboarding and MFA registration guidance should reflect the change.

Internet Access · General

Internet Access guidance documents a preview DNS-acquisition limitation

Updated guidance states that the Internet Access traffic forwarding profile does not acquire DNS traffic in preview. Wildcard acquisition rules and FQDN destinations do not enable DNS acquisition, so cloud firewall policies cannot filter DNS traffic.

Internet Access · General

New preview guidance covers cloud firewall setup for Global Secure Access clients

A new preview article explains traffic acquisition, Allow and Block firewall rules, security profiles, and enforcement verification for Global Secure Access client traffic. It also identifies the required roles, licensing, forwarding profiles, and client prerequisites.

Entra ID · Authentication

Authenticator Android backup adds passkey support

Starting in mid-January 2027, Microsoft Authenticator for Android will provide clearer backup and restore guidance and support passkeys. Users must enable Google One backup and screen lock; work and school accounts are not backed up, and backup works only in the Android personal profile. No administrator action is required.

item.title: Conditional Access policy plans preview brings shared targeting before November first-MFA registration changes — 26 October 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 26 October 2026

Conditional Access policy plans preview brings shared targeting before November first-MFA registration changes

New preview guidance covers Microsoft Entra Conditional Access policy plans, which group related rules under shared conditions and exclusions and support report-only review. A companion migration guide says existing policies remain unchanged and continue evaluating independently. Separately, a phased November 2026 rollout will let users register passkeys or passwordless sign-in as their first MFA method. The remaining additions are Secure Cloud OIDC and SCIM setup guides, while Private Access lost a connector-offline troubleshooting row.

Entra ID · Conditional Access

Conditional Access policy plans centralize conditions and exclusions in preview

The new preview guide covers creating plans from templates or from scratch, configuring shared conditions and exclusions, reviewing rules in report-only mode, and enabling plans. Creating, modifying, or deleting a plan requires the Conditional Access Administrator role.

Entra ID · Conditional Access

First-MFA registration will allow passkeys and passwordless sign-in

Microsoft Entra will let users register a passkey or passwordless sign-in as their first multifactor authentication method, removing the prior requirement to set up alternate MFA methods first. The phased rollout begins in November 2026.

Entra ID · Standards

Secure Cloud OIDC SSO setup gains a dedicated Entra guide

The new guide covers prerequisites, consent-based onboarding, authentication settings, fallback passwords, and SSO verification. It specifies that the enterprise application is created only after the initial Microsoft Entra sign-in and consent.

Entra ID · Provisioning

Secure Cloud SCIM provisioning guidance covers the full user lifecycle

The new tutorial explains automatic user and group provisioning, updates, synchronization, and deprovisioning through SCIM 2.0, including prerequisites, credentials, and deployment scope.

Private Access · General

Private Access operations guidance drops connector-offline troubleshooting

The operations page no longer includes the connector offline condition row, related Sentinel analytics guidance, or the Windows service check. Administrators should avoid relying on that removed troubleshooting workflow.

item.title: Provisioning connection cleanup joins cross-tenant agent safeguards in Entra guidance — 23 October 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 23 October 2026

Provisioning connection cleanup joins cross-tenant agent safeguards in Entra guidance

The strongest additions are provisioning-focused: new Microsoft Graph beta guidance covers inspecting and removing stored source-to-target connections, while a new HR timeout article traces delays across HR retrieval, provisioning agents, and on-premises Active Directory. Other meaningful updates clarify cross-tenant consequences for Agent ID blueprints, device- and browser-dependent passkey prompts, and DNS and site prerequisites for Cloud Sync. Global Secure Access changes are mainly navigation updates for Explicit Forward Proxy settings.

Entra ID · Provisioning

Microsoft Graph beta guidance covers stored provisioning connections

New Entra ID guidance explains how to inspect or remove stored source-to-target connections for provisioning jobs. It identifies required identifiers and permissions, includes recovery steps, and states that deleting a connection does not delete either object.

Entra ID · Troubleshooting

HR provisioning timeout troubleshooting now spans the full integration path

A new article covers intermittent timeouts and slow provisioning from Workday, SAP SuccessFactors, and API-driven HR integrations to on-premises Active Directory. Its checklist covers job status, provisioning agents, matching attributes, domain controllers, DNS, connectivity, logs, and required roles.

Agent ID · General

Disabling a multi-tenant Agent ID blueprint can affect other tenants

The updated procedure uses Disable > Disable in all tenants and specifies that related agents in other tenants can fail or lose functionality when a multi-tenant blueprint is globally disabled.

Entra ID · Authentication

System-preferred authentication now explains device-specific passkey prompts

The authentication guidance now explains that system-preferred authentication considers the current device and browser, prioritizes accessible local passkeys, and handles Windows Hello for Business and macOS Platform SSO device-bound credentials by platform.

Entra ID · General

Cloud Sync prerequisites link failures to DNS and Active Directory site mapping

The prerequisites now identify incorrect DNS, subnet-to-site mappings, and site configuration as causes of synchronization failures, performance issues, and intermittent connectivity. They direct administrators to map agent-server subnets correctly in Active Directory Sites and Services.

item.title: New revoked-credential diagnostics and Netskope coexistence guidance expand Entra admin coverage — 22 October 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 22 October 2026

New revoked-credential diagnostics and Netskope coexistence guidance expand Entra admin coverage

The period’s most consequential changes are a new Workload ID troubleshooting guide and expanded Netskope coexistence guidance for Global Secure Access and Internet Access. Microsoft also announced staged usability improvements for Microsoft Authenticator on iOS and Android. The remaining updates are lower-impact directory and numbering maintenance, including a new Fortytwo migration-partner listing and a corrected Edgile link.

Workload ID · Troubleshooting

Workload ID adds revoked-credential troubleshooting

A new guide documents revoked-credential error codes, inspection of tokenRevocations on applications and service principals through Microsoft Graph beta, and ways to assess revocation effects and possible compromise. It notes that existing tokens may continue granting access to some resources until they expire.

Internet Access · Security

Netskope guidance defines a split between private, Microsoft 365, and internet traffic

Updated coexistence guidance documents a scenario in which Global Secure Access handles private application and Microsoft 365 traffic while Netskope captures internet traffic. It adds configuration, verification, and traffic-testing steps for Windows and macOS, including forwarding profiles, steering exceptions, client settings, and traffic-log validation.

Entra ID · Authentication

Authenticator usability improvements are scheduled across iOS and Android

Microsoft says Authenticator improvements begin in October 2026, with a refreshed home experience, clearer account-restoration guidance, enhanced restoration flows, and platform-specific prompts. Android updates are scheduled to follow in November 2026 and January 2027; no organizational action is required.

item.title: Cloud Sync migration guidance now flags Device Sync as a guided-tool blocker — 21 October 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 21 October 2026

Cloud Sync migration guidance now flags Device Sync as a guided-tool blocker

Cloud Sync migration is the period’s central theme: guidance now defines guided-tool eligibility, active-server requirements, Device Sync limitations, validation steps, and safe phased coexistence. Separately, Microsoft added a Private Access and Infoblox Threat Defense configuration how-to and expanded Identity Protection and disabled-application guidance with concrete administrator implications.

Entra ID · General

Migration readiness now includes Device Sync and a two-week validation window

The guide now says migration must begin from the active Connect Sync server, treats Device Sync as a guided-migration blocker, explains readiness results, and adds validation and support-evidence checklists. It also tells administrators to keep Connect Sync installed during the two-week validation period and use tenant-specific migration dates.

Entra ID · Monitoring

Cloud Sync coexistence guidance sets a same-object export boundary

Connect Sync and Cloud Sync may coexist during a phased migration, but they must not simultaneously export normal changes for the same object and attribute set. Administrators should complete migration and reference validation before removing objects from Connect Sync scope, avoiding unintended reference removals.

Private Access · Security

New Private Access–Infoblox guidance joins DNS and private-app setup

A new how-to covers prerequisites, DNS bypasses, internal domains, category filters, endpoint groups, and security policies for using Microsoft Entra Private Access with Infoblox Threat Defense. The documented setup supports private application traffic alongside DNS security.

ID Protection · Fundamentals

Identity Protection documents risk from suspiciously added authentication methods

The page now describes a real-time Identity Protection detection for suspiciously added authentication methods. It says the detection raises user risk and can trigger configured risk-based policies, and lists Microsoft Entra ID P2 as required pending confirmation.

Entra ID · Security

Disabled-app guidance rules out accountEnabled reactivation

The consent-phishing guidance says tenant administrators cannot reverse Microsoft disablement by setting `accountEnabled` to `true` or reactivating the app registration. It directs application publishers and users to the applicable support guidance.

item.title: App Governance permissions will align with Defender XDR in mid-November — 20 October 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 20 October 2026

App Governance permissions will align with Defender XDR in mid-November

Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps will change App Governance permissions for selected Microsoft Entra roles starting in mid-November 2026. The period also adds identity-verification integration guidance for External ID, documents the irreversible nature of the Private Access v2 switch, and expands OIDC App Gallery validation guidance. Remaining updates are primarily link and ownership metadata changes.

Entra ID · Governance

Defender for Cloud Apps will change App Governance role permissions

Starting in mid-November 2026, App Governance permissions for the Cloud App Security, Compliance Administrator, and Compliance Data Administrator Microsoft Entra roles will be aligned with Defender XDR role-based access control. Administrators should review and update role assignments as needed.

Private Access · General

Private Access v2 switching is documented as non-reversible

The Manage Private Access Profile guidance now states that switching to v2 cannot be undone. Existing configurations carry over, and the change does not alter end-user traffic.

External ID · Security

New External ID guidance compares three identity-verification patterns

The new article compares Verified ID credentials, direct REST API claims, and OIDC federation, including partner-based proofing, External ID authentication, setup considerations, privacy and credential considerations, and longer-running verification journeys.

Entra ID · Standards

OIDC App Gallery validation now covers single-tenant and multitenant apps

The validation guidance now addresses both application models, with configuration-specific endpoint requirements and eligibility guidance. Teams should use the section matching their architecture and verify scopes, endpoints, and redirect URIs.

ID Governance · Governance

Entitlement Management Reports guidance separates API and portal review paths

The reports page now links to the Microsoft Graph accessDriftSummary API and separately identifies review through the Microsoft Entra admin center.

item.title: macOS SMB setup now requires a lowercase cifs identifier URI — 19 October 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 19 October 2026

macOS SMB setup now requires a lowercase cifs identifier URI

The most actionable update affects Entra ID’s macOS Platform SSO Kerberos configuration: the storage-account app registration must use a lowercase `cifs` identifier URI because uppercase `CIFS` prevents SMB mounting. Global Secure Access release notes add several client-behavior entries, while SAP IAG wording drops the “(Preview)” label and a Message Center update says recipients can disregard the Security Copilot notice.

Entra ID · Authentication

macOS Kerberos guidance makes the lowercase `cifs` requirement explicit

The updated Entra ID configuration guidance expands access from limited availability, refreshes setup links, and clarifies that the storage-account app registration must use a lowercase `cifs` identifier URI for SMB mounting on macOS. An uppercase `CIFS` value prevents the share from mounting.

Global Secure Access · General

Global Secure Access notes add client behavior and rollout details

The release notes now cover Web sign-in support, Conditional Access sign-in frequency for Private Access applications, updated firewall behavior, clearer forwarding-profile names, and private-network bypass changes. Administrators are directed to review the updated client behavior and the gradual rollout of sign-in frequency support.

ID Governance · Governance

SAP IAG page removes the “(Preview)” label

The Microsoft Entra SAP IAG integration page title and heading no longer include “(Preview).”

ID Governance · Microsoft identity platform

Message Center says the Security Copilot notice can be disregarded

The updated message says the Security Copilot inclusion notice did not reach its intended audience and can safely be disregarded.

item.title: Customer sign-in guidance says provider removal blocks signup and invitation redemption — 16 October 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 16 October 2026

Customer sign-in guidance says provider removal blocks signup and invitation redemption

Five Microsoft Learn revisions shaped the period. The most consequential update clarifies that customer sign-in identity-provider buttons cannot be hidden: removing a provider from a user flow prevents signup or invitation redemption with that provider, and `domain_hint` does not change the outcome. Other changes remove detailed Security Defaults management guidance, revise governance license mappings, and update federation examples.

Entra ID · Authentication

Customer sign-in provider removal blocks signup and invitation redemption

The FAQ now says identity-provider buttons cannot be hidden. Removing a provider from a user flow prevents users from signing up or redeeming invitations with that provider, and `domain_hint` does not change this behavior. Review flows before removing a provider.

Entra ID · Fundamentals

Security Defaults article removes individual-protection management guidance

The article no longer includes the section covering individual protections, their preview availability, roles, behavior, and management steps. Administrators relying on the article will no longer find that guidance there.

ID Governance · Fundamentals

Governance licensing guidance updates Microsoft 365 entitlement mappings

The licensing fundamentals page now maps P1 to Microsoft 365 E3, E5, or E7; P2 to E5 or E7; and Governance capabilities to Microsoft Entra Suite and Microsoft 365 E7. The agent identity licensing reference was also updated.

ID Governance · Governance

Application governance licensing guidance counts governed member users

The updated guidance says a tenant needs at least as many licenses as governed member, or non-guest, users. The count includes users who request, approve, or review application access.

External ID · General

Federation issuer example uses the source tenant’s primary domain

The user-creation example replaces the source tenant ID with its primary domain name in the issuer value and defines the new placeholder with an example domain. Administrators following the example should use the primary-domain format.

item.description:
Day in brief · 12 October 2026

Passkey campaign guidance separates platform nudges, attestation paths, and silent SSO

Campaign profiles have clearer platform-specific nudge rules

The guidance says unrestricted, synced-only, and device-bound-only profiles use platform-specific evaluation. AAGUID-restricted and attestation-enforced profiles suppress nudges across platforms after one eligible passkey is registered.

The guidance states that Windows Hello for Business registration doesn’t follow passkey profile restrictions, so administrators should evaluate it separately when interpreting nudge suppression.

item.description:

The strongest changes affect trust authentication, Conditional Access scoping, and Agent ID troubleshooting. Updated What's New guidance describes key rotation for incoming trust referral flows as generally available, improving reliability and addressing failures when referral tickets use a secondary key. Entra ID · Authentication

Entra ID · Conditional Access

item.description:

item.description:
Day in brief · 6 October 2026

Cloud Sync supports hybrid-join device synchronization; Private Access 2.2.79 adds OTA updates

The most consequential updates clarify Cloud Sync support for Microsoft Entra hybrid join and document the Private Access Sensor 2.2.79 release, including its upgrade prerequisites. Entra administrators also get a more precise SSPR authentication-method count and stronger External ID passkey sample warnings. Most other changes were spelling, metadata, naming, or presentation edits.

Entra ID · Provisioning

Cloud Sync migration now includes hybrid-join device synchronization

The migration decision guide now states that Cloud Sync supports device synchronization for Microsoft Entra hybrid join. Device synchronization must be enabled separately, with updated migration guidance and configuration steps. Administrators moving hybrid-joined devices should include this capability explicitly in their migration plan.

Private Access · General

Private Access Sensor 2.2.79 adds OTA updates and Kerberos improvements

The release history records version 2.2.79, released September 29, 2026, with over-the-air sensor updates, enhanced Kerberos security and diagnostics, SID-based service matching, and corrected wildcard matching. Upgrading from version 2.2.42 requires a one-time full-installer deployment to enable OTA updates; inbound TCP and UDP port 1337 must be allowed, and IPv4 is required because IPv6 Kerberos traffic is blocked.

Entra ID · Authentication

SSPR counts Authenticator and OATH variants as one method

The SSPR guidance now states that Microsoft Authenticator, software OATH tokens, and hardware OATH tokens count as one authentication method, regardless of Authentication methods policy migration status. Administrators should use that shared count when evaluating SSPR method requirements.

External ID · Authentication

External ID passkey samples receive explicit high-privilege warnings

The updated guidance describes administrator-controlled passkey provisioning through the FIDO2 provisioning APIs and identifies the sample as testing-only. Its deletion flow uses high-privilege permissions and a client secret in browser code, so the sample should not be deployed in production.

External ID · Authentication

External-tenant SMS guidance distinguishes first-factor and SSPR use

The FAQ now states that SMS is unavailable for first-factor authentication in external tenants while indicating availability for self-service password reset. SMS remains available for second-factor verification at additional cost, giving administrators a clearer basis for external-tenant SSPR planning.

item.title: SharePoint OTP retirement, Connect deadlines, and app-gallery onboarding reshape Entra administration — 1 October 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 1 October 2026

SharePoint OTP retirement, Connect deadlines, and app-gallery onboarding reshape Entra administration

SharePoint One-Time Passcode authentication will retire across Microsoft 365 tenants starting in mid-October 2026, moving external sharing to Microsoft Entra B2B. Microsoft also opened self-service App Gallery onboarding in public preview ahead of general availability in mid-November, while Connect guidance separates a new AD FS/PingFederate hardening requirement from the broader Sync upgrade deadline.

External ID · Conditional Access

SharePoint OTP moves external sharing to Entra B2B in mid-October

SharePoint One-Time Passcode authentication will retire starting in mid-October 2026 for all Microsoft 365 tenants. External users will need guest accounts under Microsoft Entra B2B, bringing SharePoint and OneDrive sharing under consistent governance and Conditional Access.

Entra ID · Standards

App Gallery opens self-service onboarding ahead of November GA

ISVs can now validate SSO and provisioning integrations, manage submissions, and track status in the Microsoft Entra admin center. The capability is in public preview, with general availability beginning in mid-November 2026.

Workload ID · Provisioning

AD FS and PingFederate hardening raises the Connect minimum

The documented requirement changes from Microsoft Entra Connect 2.5.79.0 to 2.6.84.0 or later. Application-based authentication is also required to maintain directory synchronization and avoid service disruptions.

Entra ID · Provisioning

General Connect Sync upgrade deadline moves to April 2027

The minimum-version deadline shifts from September 30, 2026, to April 7, 2027. Microsoft Entra Connect Sync 2.5.79.0 or later is required; synchronization services will fail until the upgrade is completed if the requirement is missed.

Workload ID · Authentication

SAP workload identities now require a matching API host

The updated guide removes its Preview label and states that workload identities are reusable only when their Application API host matches the provisioning app’s SAP SuccessFactors API host. It also adds the Application ID URI format and compatibility details for the September 15, 2026 update.

item.title: Chatwork SCIM provisioning ends October 1, 2026 as Entra sharpens agent-access guidance — 30 September 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 30 September 2026

Chatwork SCIM provisioning ends October 1, 2026 as Entra sharpens agent-access guidance

Administrators using the Chatwork Enterprise App Gallery integration face a stated October 1, 2026 cutoff: SCIM provisioning will stop, and the integration will no longer provision users. The period also substantially expands Agent ID Conditional Access guidance around token subjects, agent-user targeting, prerequisites, and report-only rollout. Global Secure Access guidance records a Secure DNS limitation, while most remaining edits cover wording, links, terminology, or role documentation.

Entra ID · Provisioning

Chatwork provisioning support has a firm October 1 cutoff

The Chatwork Provisioning Tutorial now states that SCIM provisioning support will end on October 1, 2026. After that date, the Microsoft Entra Enterprise App Gallery integration will stop provisioning users. The page also standardizes the product name to “Chatwork.”

Agent ID · Conditional Access

Agent Conditional Access guidance now separates three identity patterns

The guidance distinguishes agents acting for signed-in users, agents using their own identity, and agents using an agent user account. It adds separate guidance links for autonomous agents and agent users and updates the listed licensing combinations, giving administrators a basis for selecting the relevant policy guidance.

Agent ID · Conditional Access

Autonomous-agent policy guidance adds prerequisites and report-only rollout

The updated autonomous-agent guidance presents Conditional Access as a scenario-based pattern, adds prerequisites, and recommends starting block policies in report-only mode. It also states that an Agent 365 license will soon be required.

Entra ID · Conditional Access

Broad Conditional Access targeting does not include agent users

New guidance for securing agent users states that all-user and group targeting do not include agent users. It documents prerequisites, risk controls, device and network conditions, and blocking risky agent user accounts, so administrators should use the dedicated agent-user pattern rather than assume broad targeting covers these accounts.

Global Secure Access · General

Global Secure Access documents Secure DNS and macOS tunneling limits

The known-limitations guidance now states that the Global Secure Access client does not support Secure DNS variants including DoH, DoT, and DNSSEC. It also says the macOS client bypasses Secure DNS to enforce FQDN-based tunneling.

item.title: Connect Sync guidance sets a 2.6.84.0 minimum and April 7, 2027 authentication deadline — 29 September 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 29 September 2026

Connect Sync guidance sets a 2.6.84.0 minimum and April 7, 2027 authentication deadline

Most of the period is low-impact documentation maintenance involving terminology, metadata, links, and examples. The meaningful administrator-facing changes are updated Connect Sync requirements, removal of the Cloud Sync device-sync Preview label, new GitHub federation claim guidance, clearer Kerberos prerequisites, and more precise PIM eligibility duration behavior.

Entra ID · Security

Connect Sync guidance raises the minimum to 2.6.84.0

The updated Security Updates Pks guidance changes the stated required version from 2.5.79.0 to 2.6.84.0 or later. It also requires application-based authentication by April 7, 2027; synchronization services stop after that date when either requirement is unmet.

Entra ID · Provisioning

Cloud Sync device sync loses its Preview designation

The device-sync article removes the Preview label and preview legal notice, while also updating its publication date. The supplied guidance specifies no administrator action.

Workload ID · Security

GitHub federation guidance adopts immutable repository subject claims

Starting July 15, 2026, GitHub automatically uses immutable subject claims for newly created, renamed, or transferred repositories. Existing repositories retain name-based claims unless they opt in.

Workload ID · Authentication

Kerberos guidance separates directory provisioning from passwordless access

Users and groups provisioned to Active Directory with Cloud Sync can access Kerberos-protected resources through Microsoft Entra Kerberos, Windows Hello for Business, or FIDO2. Provisioning alone does not enable Kerberos or passwordless access.

ID Governance · Governance

PIM documents 365-day expiration for eligible assignments

The `duration: P365D` value makes an eligible assignment expire after 365 days. Permanent eligibility requires the target scope's role-management policy to allow it.

item.title: Global Secure Access connector guidance defines non-overlapping TCP ranges — 28 September 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 28 September 2026

Global Secure Access connector guidance defines non-overlapping TCP ranges

All 11 entries were Microsoft Learn updates. The substantive changes tighten Global Secure Access connector port guidance, clarify the weakness of device-platform signals in Conditional Access, and revise Exchange role-assignment instructions; several other pages contain Workplace or Meta Workplace reference cleanup.

Global Secure Access · Fundamentals

Connectors get explicit dynamic and AutoReuse TCP ranges

Global Secure Access connector guidance specifies non-overlapping dynamic TCP ports 49152–65535 and AutoReuse TCP ports 10000–49151. It adds Windows Server 2016+ prerequisites and configuration and verification commands, and clarifies that AutoReuse applies only to TCP.

Entra ID · Conditional Access

Conditional Access guidance warns that device-platform data is unverified

The conditions guidance says device-platform information, including user-agent strings, can be modified and is not verified. It recommends combining device-platform conditions with Microsoft Intune device-compliance policies or using them in a block statement.

Entra ID · Fundamentals

Exchange role assignments through dynamic groups move to updated guidance

The groups guidance directs administrators to the Exchange admin center for role assignments through dynamic membership groups. When the old Exchange admin center is required, it says to assign the eligible role directly to the user rather than through role-assignable groups; Exchange PowerShell cmdlets continue to work as expected.

Entra ID · Standards

Partner-driven integration examples add Dropbox and Snowflake

The partner-driven integrations page now lists Dropbox and Snowflake as examples and removes its reference to Workplace by Facebook. No configuration change is indicated.
